title: Platform Systems & Services: Playbook, Dashboards, Runbooks, Roadmap (2029 Q1)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical playbook for Redwood's Platform Systems & Services (PSS). It combines a service inventory, SLOs, dashboard and alert conventions, on-call runbooks for common incidents, how-tos for platform operators, a near-term roadmap for Q1 2029, and a short retrospective of Q4 2028 work and follow-ups. Audience: platform engineers, SREs, service owners, and on-call responders.

Scope and purpose:
- Covers core platform services (control plane APIs, routing, orchestration, metrics & logging, secrets management, deployment pipelines, and core infra tooling).
- Prescribes alert thresholds, dashboard templates, incident runbooks, and ownership.
- Defines the roadmap items and success criteria for Q1 2029.

Ownership and contacts:
- Platform systems owner: "platform-systems-team@redwood.ai" (primary).
- On-call rotation: platform-sre primary, platform-oncall secondary. PagerDuty rotations: PSS-Platform-Prod (primary), PSS-Platform-Infra (secondary).
- Escalation matrix:
  1. On-call engineer (P1/P2 initial responder) — 15 minutes SLA to acknowledge.
  2. Sr. SRE (if unresolved after 30 minutes) — page.
  3. Engineering manager and product owner (if business impact > 30 minutes).

Service inventory (summary):
- control-plane-api: API gateway for product-facing platform services. Owner: eng-platform/control-plane. SLO: 99.95% availability, p99 latency < 120ms for 256B requests.
- model-router: Smart routing service for inference requests and fallbacks. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. SLO: 99.9% availability, p95 latency < 200ms.
- job-orchestrator: Batch and cron job scheduler used by data and infra teams. Owner: eng-platform/schedulers. SLO: 99.8% successful job starts within 5m.
- secrets-store: Central KMS/KV for platform secrets (integrates with HSM). Owner: security-and-compliance. SLO: 99.99% availability for reads, latency < 50ms.
- metrics-logging: Prometheus + Loki + Cortex stack for metrics/logs. Owner: eng-platform/observability. SLO: 99% retention and query availability for 90d.

SLOs and key metrics (example table):
- control-plane-api: availability: 99.95% (monthly), alert: availability < 99.9% for 10m.
- control-plane-api: p99 latency < 120ms, alert: p99 > 200ms for 5m and error rate > 1%.
- model-router: error rate < 0.5%, alert: error rate > 1% sustained 5m.
- job-orchestrator: queue-depth < 1000, alert: queue-depth > 2000 or median job-start-delay > 5m.

Dashboards and alerts (conventions & examples):
- Dashboard naming convention: PSS / <service> / <purpose> (e.g., PSS / control-plane-api / prod-overview).
- Panels to include on every prod overview dashboard:
  - Availability (% successful requests, 1m/5m/1h).
  - Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) split by endpoint.
  - Error rate (4xx/5xx) and common error messages.
  - Dependency health (secrets-store, model-router availability).
  - Request throughput (rps) and concurrency.

Alerting conventions (Grafana Alertmanager + Prometheus rules):
- Alert severity labels: sev:page (P1/P2), sev:notify (P3), sev:info (P4).
- Typical rule example (PromQL):
  - name: ControlPlaneHighP99
    expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="control-plane-api"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.2
    for: 5m
    labels: { severity: "page" }
    annotations: { runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/control-plane-high-latency-2029-q1" }

- Escalation policy: alerts labeled severity=page route to PagerDuty PSS-Platform-Prod. Notification policy requires acknowledgment within 15 minutes.

Runbooks (selected):
1) control-plane-api - High latency / partial outage (P1)
  - Symptoms: elevated p99 > 200ms, increase in 5xx errors, degraded downstream requests to model-router.
  - Immediate steps:
    1. Acknowledge pager and post a short summary to #platform-incident with timestamp, incident id.
    2. Check control-plane-api prod dashboard and note spike time range.
    3. Check recent deploys (CI/CD) in the last 30m: `gh workflow view --repo redwood/control-plane --help` then `gh run list --status completed --limit 5` (replace with org commands).
    4. Verify model-router health: `kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=model-router` and `kubectl logs -f <pod> --since=10m` for immediate errors.
    5. If errors show OOM or GPU scheduling failures, scale up model-router pool: `kubectl scale deployment model-router --replicas=4 -n platform` and notify SRE.
    6. If errors are due to upstream secrets-store, check KMS latency and rotate to fallback region (see secrets-store runbook).
  - Mitigations and rollback:
    - If a recent deploy correlates with onset, perform a canary rollback via the CI/CD rollback job: `./scripts/rollback-deploy.sh control-plane-api prod --to-last-stable`
  - Post-incident actions:
    - Open incident review ticket in JIRA with timeline, root cause, actions, and assign to owner.
    - Update runbook with missing steps or broken checks.

2) metrics-logging - Prometheus scrape failures / missing metrics (P2)
  - Symptoms: missing series for key metrics, Cortex write errors, Loki errors for ingestion backlog.
  - Steps:
    1. Check Prometheus targets page and scrape_latency_seconds.
    2. Check Cortex ingesters and ring status: `kubectl get pods -n observability` and `curl -s http://cortex-ingester:8080/metrics`
    3. If disk pressure is observed, scale PVC or rotate older metric retention buckets.
    4. If Cortex write errors persist, enable write-fallback to warm storage and file a follow-up.

How-tos (operational recipes):
- Add a new dashboard from template:
  1. Duplicate the canonical PSS dashboard JSON in Grafana (folder: PSS / templates).
  2. Edit variables: cluster, namespace, service_name.
  3. Save with name: PSS / <service> / prod-overview and set folder permissions to team=platform.

- Create a new alert rule:
  1. Add a PrometheusRule in git: `infra/observability/prometheus-rules/<service>-alerts.yaml` following our alert template header.
  2. Run CI check: `make observability-lint` to validate PromQL and labels.
  3. Submit PR and request reviewers from eng-platform and eng-sre.
  4. Once merged, the rule auto-deploys via the observability-controller. Verify with: `kubectl get prometheusrules -n observability` and check new alerts in Grafana.

- On-call playbook for creating a short-lived hotfix branch and canary deploy:
  1. Branch: `git checkout -b hotfix/control-plane-<short-desc>`
  2. Cherry-pick commit(s) and run unit tests: `make test` and `make integration-test --filter=smoke`
  3. Build image and push with tag `hotfix-<timestamp>`: `ci/build-and-push.sh control-plane-api hotfix-<timestamp>`
  4. Trigger canary deploy via the CI/CD canary job and monitor control-plane-api/canary dashboard for 15m.

Roadmap (Q1 2029 - objectives and success criteria):
- Objective: Improve control-plane availability during high-load model fallbacks.
  - Initiative: Circuit-breaker improvements to model-router and enhanced fallback routing. Success: p99 latency reduction by 20% under synthetic 2x load tests; verified by blue-green test.
- Objective: Reduce MTTR for infra incidents affecting metrics and logging.
  - Initiative: Automate observability self-heal playbooks (auto-scale Cortex ingesters, rotate storage). Success: MTTR reduction from median 48m -> 20m in runbook-measured incidents.
- Objective: Standardize dashboard templates and importability for partner teams.
  - Initiative: Publish Grafana dashboard-as-code templates and onboarding guide. Success: 5 partner teams adopt templates in Q1.

Retrospective (Q4 2028 highlights and follow-ups):
- Incident: 2028-11-21 control-plane API partial outage (root cause: memory leak in routing table manager).
  - Action taken: emergency rollback, patch release, improved GC and connection pooling.
  - Follow-ups: add heap utilization panel, introduce memory-based autoscale for control-plane-api.
- Incident: 2028-12-09 metrics ingestion backlog (root cause: Cortex compactor misconfiguration).
  - Action taken: compactor config rolled back and compactor pod restarts.
  - Follow-ups: add compactor liveness/readiness checks and automated compactor config validation in CI.

Operational KPIs (monthly):
- Mean Time To Acknowledge (MTTA) target: <= 10 minutes.
- Mean Time To Resolve (MTTR) target for P1: <= 60 minutes.
- Change failure rate target: <= 2% for production rollouts.

Appendix A — Useful queries and snippets:
- PromQL: control_plane_error_rate = sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane-api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane-api"}[5m]))
- Grafana panel JSON: use templates in `infra/observability/grafana/templates/control-plane-overview.json` (example stored in git).
- Alertmanager route example:
  routes:
    - match:
        severity: "page"
      receiver: "pagerduty-p1"
      continue: false

Appendix B — Runbook ownership and maintenance policy:
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly by the owner listed at top.
- Post-incident, the on-call responder must file a postmortem within 72 hours for any P1/P2 and include updates to runbook steps.
- All runbooks live in the confluence runbooks folder and also mirrored in the `infra/runbooks` git repo as markdown.

References and links:
- Observability standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards
- Incident response playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process
- Grafana templates repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-observability.git

Change log:
- 2029-01-08: Created (Aisha Patel).
- 2029-02-10: Published edits after Q4 retrospective; added PromQL examples and updated alert thresholds.

If you are new to the platform team: follow the Quickstart onboarding checklist in the team wiki and request platform access via the access-and-permissions form in the policies section.
